authors: Charles S. Oakes, John M. Simonson, Robert J. Bodnar
title: Apparent Molar Volumes of Aqueous Calcium Chloride to 250 C, 400 bars, and from Molalities of 0.242 to 6.150
experimental_method: Relative densities of CaCl2(aq) (0.242 to 6.150 mol/kg) measured against water with two high-pressure vibrating-tube densimeters at 25 to 250 C and near 70 and 400 bar; tubes calibrated with H2O-D2O, H2O-NaCl(aq) and H2O-Ar pairs; stock solutions made from CaCl2.2H2O, the 6.150 m stock analysed by desiccation and by 25 C density.
uncertainties_stated: Table V gives upper limits on the statistical error of the density difference (10^6 d_rho_err: 170, 200, 200, 250, 300, 400 at 25, 50, 100, 150, 200, 250 C; exceptions 300 at 2.7917 m (50 C), 1200 at 3.8402 m and 650 at 4.9573 m (100 C)) and of V_phi (0.1, 0.3, 0.4, 0.4, 0.4, 0.6 cm3/mol at the lowest molality); the authors say errors in calibrating-fluid densities were ignored so d_rho errors are understated. Stock-solution molality 6.150+-0.005.
quality_remarks: The printed pressure of a nominal 70 or 400 bar block varies from row to row (e.g. 70.3-73.8 bar at 25 C, 405-411 bar at 200-250 C); each row's own printed pressure is used. Apparent molar volume V_phi is the authors' calculation; the measured density difference is in the last column. Printed values that look inconsistent, kept as printed: 249.76 C, 71.4 bar, 1.4990 m has rho0 = 0.803081 (six decimals) and 10^3 d_rho = 52.72 (neighbouring molalities 106.31 at 0.9867 m and 152.53 at 1.4990 m, 71.3 bar, suggest 152.72 was intended); 149.82 C, 71.0 bar, m printed as 0.242 (three decimals) with V_phi = 18.29, far above the trend (10.57 at 0.4873 m, 12.68 at 0.7354 m); 249.80 C, 405.0 bar, 0.2416 m has 10^3 d_rho = 26.6 (one decimal). These are likely misprints in the paper, not extraction errors (confirmed on the page image). Highest-temperature low-molality V_phi values are strongly negative and error-sensitive. Header in the 1995 volume: J. Solution Chem. Vol. 24, No. 9, p. 897 on.
